# 1 Kings Chapter 19 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
**2** Then Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, "So may the gods do to me and more also, if I do not make your life as the life of one of them by this time tomorrow."
**3** Then he was afraid, and he arose and ran for his life and came to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah, and left his servant there.
**4** But he himself went a day's journey into the wilderness and came and sat down under a broom tree. And he asked that he might die, saying, "It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life, for I am no better than my fathers."
**5** And he lay down and slept under a broom tree. And behold, an angel touched him and said to him, "Arise and eat."
**6** And he looked, and behold, there was at his head a cake baked on hot stones and a jar of water. And he ate and drank and lay down again.
**7** And the angel of the LORD came again a second time and touched him and said, "Arise and eat, for the journey is too great for you."
**8** And he arose and ate and drank, and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mount of God.
**9** There he came to a cave and lodged in it. And behold, the word of the LORD came to him, and he said to him, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"
**10** He said, "I have been very jealous for the LORD, the God of hosts. For the people of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword, and I, even I only, am left, and they seek my life, to take it away."
**11** And he said, "Go out and stand on the mount before the LORD." And behold, the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind tore the mountains and broke in pieces the rocks before the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind. And after the wind an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake.
**12** And after the earthquake a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire. And after the fire the sound of a low whisper.
**13** And when Elijah heard it, he wrapped his face in his cloak and went out and stood at the entrance of the cave. And behold, there came a voice to him and said, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"
**14** He said, "I have been very jealous for the LORD, the God of hosts. For the people of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword, and I, even I only, am left, and they seek my life, to take it away."
**15** And the LORD said to him, "Go, return on your way to the wilderness of Damascus. And when you arrive, you shall anoint Hazael to be king over Syria.
**16** And Jehu the son of Nimshi you shall anoint to be king over Israel, and Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah you shall anoint to be prophet in your place.
**17** And the one who escapes from the sword of Hazael shall Jehu put to death, and the one who escapes from the sword of Jehu shall Elisha put to death.
**18** Yet I will leave seven thousand in Israel, all the knees that have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him."
**19** So he departed from there and found Elisha the son of Shaphat, who was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen in front of him, and he was with the twelfth. Elijah passed by him and cast his cloak upon him.
**20** And he left the oxen and ran after Elijah and said, "Let me kiss my father and my mother, and then I will follow you." And he said to him, "Go back again, for what have I done to you?"
**21** And he returned from following him and took the yoke of oxen and sacrificed them and boiled their flesh with the yokes of the oxen and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he arose and went after Elijah and assisted him.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA has reviewed the translations of EMET (literal), LOGOS (formal), and PNEUMA (dynamic) for this chapter.

**Method**: Each verse was compared across all three translations. The LOGOS formal translation serves as the primary consensus baseline, with adjustments where EMET's literalism reveals important Hebrew features or PNEUMA's dynamic rendering better captures the original intent.

## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

**Chapter 19**: 13 verse(s) with significant divergence

### Verse 2
- **EMET**: And-Jezebel sent a-messenger to-Elijah, saying, "Thus may-the-gods do to-me and-thus may-they-add, if by-this time tomorrow I-do-not make your-life as-the-life-of one-of-them."
- **LOGOS**: Then Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, "So may the gods do to me and more also, if I do not make your life as the life of one of them by this time tomorrow."
- **PNEUMA**: Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah: "May the gods strike me dead if by this time tomorrow I haven't done to you what you did to them."
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 3
- **EMET**: And-he-saw, and-he-arose, and-went for-his-life, and-came to-Beer-sheba, that belongs-to-Judah, and-left his-servant there.
- **LOGOS**: Then he was afraid, and he arose and ran for his life and came to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah, and left his servant there.
- **PNEUMA**: Elijah was terrified. He ran for his life, all the way to Beersheba in Judah, where he left his servant behind.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 4
- **EMET**: And-he went into-the-wilderness a-day's journey, and-came and-sat under a-broom-bush, and-asked ʾet-his-soul to-die, and-said, "Enough! Now, YHWH, take my-life, for I-am-not better than-my-fathers."
- **LOGOS**: But he himself went a day's journey into the wilderness and came and sat down under a broom tree. And he asked that he might die, saying, "It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life, for I am no bet...
- **PNEUMA**: Then he went a day's journey into the desert, sat down under a broom bush, and prayed to die. "I've had enough, LORD," he said. "Take my life. I'm no better than my ancestors."
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 5
- **EMET**: And-he-lay-down and-slept under a-broom-bush. And-behold — an-angel touching-him, and-said to-him, "Arise, eat."
- **LOGOS**: And he lay down and slept under a broom tree. And behold, an angel touched him and said to him, "Arise and eat."
- **PNEUMA**: He lay down under the bush and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel touched him and said, "Get up and eat."
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 10
- **EMET**: And-he-said, "I-have-been-very-zealous for-YHWH, the-God-of Hosts, for the-sons-of Israel have-forsaken your-covenant, ʾet-your-altars they-have-torn-down, and-ʾet-your-prophets they-have-killed with-...
- **LOGOS**: He said, "I have been very jealous for the LORD, the God of hosts. For the people of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword, and I, even I...
- **PNEUMA**: He answered, "I have been absolutely devoted to the LORD God Almighty. The Israelites have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars, and murdered your prophets. I am the only one left, and now t...
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 14
- **EMET**: And-he-said, "I-have-been-very-zealous for-YHWH, the-God-of Hosts, for the-sons-of Israel have-forsaken your-covenant, ʾet-your-altars they-have-torn-down, and-ʾet-your-prophets they-have-killed with-...
- **LOGOS**: He said, "I have been very jealous for the LORD, the God of hosts. For the people of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword, and I, even I...
- **PNEUMA**: He gave the same answer: "I have been absolutely devoted to the LORD God Almighty. The Israelites have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars, and murdered your prophets. I'm the only one left...
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 15
- **EMET**: And-YHWH said to-him, "Go, return on-your-way to the-wilderness-of Damascus. And-when-you-come, you-shall-anoint Hazael as-king over Aram.
- **LOGOS**: And the LORD said to him, "Go, return on your way to the wilderness of Damascus. And when you arrive, you shall anoint Hazael to be king over Syria.
- **PNEUMA**: The LORD told him, "Go back the way you came, through the desert to Damascus. When you get there, anoint Hazael as king of Aram.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 16
- **EMET**: And-ʾet-Jehu son-of Nimshi you-shall-anoint as-king over Israel. And-ʾet-Elisha son-of Shaphat, from-Abel-meholah, you-shall-anoint as-prophet in-your-place.
- **LOGOS**: And Jehu the son of Nimshi you shall anoint to be king over Israel, and Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah you shall anoint to be prophet in your place.
- **PNEUMA**: Anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king of Israel, and anoint Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel-meholah as the prophet who will succeed you.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 17
- **EMET**: And-it-shall-be — the-one-who-escapes from-the-sword-of Hazael, Jehu will-kill. And-the-one-who-escapes from-the-sword-of Jehu, Elisha will-kill.
- **LOGOS**: And the one who escapes from the sword of Hazael shall Jehu put to death, and the one who escapes from the sword of Jehu shall Elisha put to death.
- **PNEUMA**: Anyone who escapes Hazael's sword will be killed by Jehu, and anyone who escapes Jehu's sword will be killed by Elisha.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 18
- **EMET**: And-I-will-leave in-Israel seven thousand — all the-knees that have-not bowed to-the-Baal, and-every mouth that has-not kissed-him."
- **LOGOS**: Yet I will leave seven thousand in Israel, all the knees that have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him."
- **PNEUMA**: But I still have seven thousand in Israel — every knee that has not bowed to Baal and every mouth that has not kissed his image."
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

— SOPHIA
